title: The Revolution Devours Its Favourite Son — Eddie Would Go

u.La revolución se come a su hijo predilec: The Revolution Devours Its Favourite Son
u.La revolución conservadora que transform: The conservative revolution that reshaped the Supreme Court in order to dismantle the administrative state is now the principal obstacle to Trump's trade policy. The irony is structural, and its consequences reach far beyond tariffs.
u.«Las revoluciones que triunfan crean las: «Revolutions that succeed forge the chains their successors cannot break.»
u.— Alexis de Tocqueville, La democracia e: — Alexis de Tocqueville, Democracy in America (1835)
u.El regreso de Donald Trump al epicentro: Donald Trump's return to the epicentre of the American trade debate is not a repeat of his first term. It is a sequel staged in a theatre whose judicial rules have changed profoundly. The self-styled "Tariff Man" projects an agenda of universal, aggressive tariffs, but runs into a paradox that did not exist in 2018: the very conservative revolution that reshaped the Supreme Court in order to dismantle the "administrative state" is now the principal obstacle to the executive's discretion over trade. If in the first term presidential will navigated choppy but somewhat calmer judicial waters, today the administration resembles a captain attempting to impose a blockade with a fleet whose chain of command has been fragmented by his own courts.
u.La tensión ya no es solo política o macr: The tension is no longer merely political or macroeconomic but constitutional: a clash between an imperial vision of the presidency in foreign trade and a judiciary that has decided to reclaim its role as the final interpreter of the law — and, in consequence, to empower the legislature in the process. To understand why Trump's tariff policy is more fragile than it appears, one has to understand what happened to the so-called Chevron deference, and why its disappearance changes everything.
u.El fin de Chevron y lo que dejó en su lu: The end of Chevron and what it left behind
u.Durante cuatro décadas, la \"deferencia: For four decades, "Chevron deference" was the lubricant that allowed technical agencies — among them the Office of the United States Trade Representative, the USTR — to manoeuvre in the grey zones of trade statutes. The principle was simple: where the law was ambiguous, judges were to defer to the expert agency's interpretation rather than substitute their own. That principle died in 2024 with the ruling in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo. The Supreme Court removed the obligation on judges to accept reasonable interpretations of ambiguous laws and established a standard of independent review of legal questions.
u.Para el USTR, el impacto es sísmico. Las: For the USTR, the impact is seismic. American trade laws were deliberately drafted with an ambiguity that allowed diplomatic flexibility. That ambiguity was the room for manoeuvre. Now that room has vanished: it is a judge — not a trade policy specialist — who decides whether a statutory gap does or does not permit the imposition of a levy. Every tariff proposal becomes a process vulnerable to strict judicial scrutiny. What once took weeks of administrative processing can be suspended by a federal injunction within days.
u.La Corte de Comercio Internacional ha de: The Court of International Trade has ceased to be a passive spectator and become the arbiter of the procedural validity of the tariff instruments the administration uses most. The litigation over the so-called Lists 3 and 4A — which hit Chinese products worth hundreds of billions of dollars under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 — exposed the seams of executive power in ways that would have been unthinkable in the first term.
u.Los tribunales identificaron tres vulner: The courts identified three specific vulnerabilities. The first is procedural: under the Administrative Procedure Act, the Court found that the USTR had failed to respond adequately to the more than 28,000 public comments received while the tariffs were being processed, which invalidates the presumption of legality of the measure. The second is substantive: the executive's capacity to add products at its discretion, without investigations establishing a causal link to the original unfair practices, has been called into question. The third is the most politically significant: the courts no longer accept that a mere invocation of foreign policy or national security automatically shields a tariff decision. The substance of policy remains a presidential prerogative. The procedure is now fully justiciable.
u.La IEEPA: el último recurso y sus límite: The IEEPA: the last resort and its limits
u.Ante el asedio judicial a las herramient: Faced with the judicial siege of its ordinary tools, the executive is tempted to fall back on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, the IEEPA. Designed for situations of extreme crisis, it grants powers of almost total reach over foreign trade once a national emergency has been declared. It is, in practice, the last refuge of presidential activism in trade matters.
u.Pero la IEEPA tampoco es inmune al nuevo: But the IEEPA is not immune to the new legal climate either. The so-called Major Questions Doctrine — developed by that same conservative Supreme Court — holds that where an emergency decision carries vast economic impact and lacks a sufficiently clear legislative delegation from Congress, the courts may intervene. In other words: using the IEEPA systematically to circumvent ordinary trade controls invites an unprecedented constitutional collision. The nuclear option has its own activation code, and the courts now control part of that code.
u.El resultado práctico es una jerarquía d: The practical result is a hierarchy of vulnerability that any trade strategist must take into account. Section 301 is the most exposed tool: it faces exhaustive judicial review and a requirement of reasoned justification under the Administrative Procedure Act. Section 232 — which permits tariffs on national security grounds — is somewhat more robust, but the courts have begun to question expansive definitions of security that reach beyond the strictly military. The IEEPA is the most protected, but precisely for that reason its systematic use to bypass the other routes accumulates the greatest long-term political and constitutional risk.
u.Lo que esto significa más allá de las fr: What this means beyond the border
u.La fricción entre el despacho oval y los: The friction between the Oval Office and the courts of Washington is not a domestic affair. On the great chessboard of competition with China, the fragmentation of domestic power erodes American deterrence in a way no tariff can offset. If Beijing or Brussels calculate that a tariff announced by the president can be suspended by an injunction in a federal court, the tariff's effectiveness as bargaining currency in a negotiation is drastically reduced. The threat loses credibility the moment the adversary learns to wait for the litigation.
u.Las consecuencias sistémicas van más lej: The systemic consequences reach further. Judicial uncertainty makes economic decoupling from strategic rivals — the declared objective of trade policy — chaotic: the rules change not through deliberate strategy but through unforeseen rulings. The repeated use of emergency laws to circumvent judicial blockage accelerates, at the margin, the search for global alternatives to the American financial system — exactly the opposite of what a strong-dollar policy is meant to achieve. And while the United States ignores the WTO's dispute settlement system and its own domestic system turns hyper-litigious, global trade operates in a normative limbo that benefits, above all, whoever needs legal certainty least.
u.El futuro de la política comercial estad: The future of American trade policy will no longer be decided solely by the protectionist instinct of the executive. It will be decided, to a growing extent, by the technical skill of its lawyers in navigating a judiciary that is asserting a role of its own. The end of Chevron deference is the death certificate of the era of the blank cheque for trade agencies.
u.El mejor caso para ver el impacto que es: The clearest case for seeing the impact of this decision is the relationship with Spain, in the midst of the conflict with Iran. Before this ruling, faced with the Spanish government's refusal, one might have expected the president to respond with tweets imposing tariffs on products exported by Madrid. But that is not what happened: he threatened instead a curious commercial blockade of Spain which, as an EU member, would carry little weight. This demonstrates the impact of the ruling and the constraints it places on Trump and on foreign policy.
u.La ironía es estructural y merece ser di: The irony is structural and deserves to be stated precisely: the conservative movement that worked for decades to curtail the power of federal regulatory agencies achieved its objective. But in the process it deprived its own leader of the room for manoeuvre those agencies afforded him. The very judicial revolution that was meant to free a conservative executive from the administrative state bound it instead to a standard of scrutiny its predecessors never faced. In the present polycrisis, law is no longer a simple bureaucratic formality. It is the frontier where geopolitical ambition meets its limits. And that frontier is being drawn, with growing precision, by the very judges the conservative movement installed to do something else entirely.
